def: Application Programming Interface: rules that let one program request data or actions from another.
A specific URL where an API receives requests for one kind of resource.
HyperText Transfer Protocol: the request and response language of the web.
HTTP sent inside an encrypted TLS connection.
JavaScript Object Notation: a lightweight text format for structured data.
An API style where each resource has a URL and you act on it with HTTP methods.
An API query language where the client asks for exactly the fields it wants from one endpoint.
A three-digit number in an HTTP response saying whether the request succeeded.
A standard that lets an app act for a user with a limited token, without the user's password.
A short-lived credential an app sends to prove it is allowed to call an API.
A named container that stores a value in a program.
A reusable, named block of code that takes inputs and can return an output.
A project folder tracked by Git, including its full history.
A saved snapshot of your project in Git, with a message describing the change.
An independent line of work in Git that can later be merged.
A request on GitHub to review and merge one branch into another.
A model made of layers of simple connected units that learns patterns from examples.
A number inside a neural network that sets how strongly one unit influences another. Training adjusts weights.
The training method that nudges weights in the direction that reduces error.
The algorithm that works out how much each weight contributed to the error.
The neural network architecture behind modern LLMs, built around attention.
A mechanism that lets a model weigh how relevant every other token is when processing one token.
A chunk of text (a word or word piece) that a language model reads and writes.
A list of numbers representing meaning, so similar things have similar numbers.
Large Language Model: a neural network trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next token.
The text instructions and context you give an AI model.
The maximum number of tokens a model can consider at once, including your prompt and its reply.
When a model states something false with confidence.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: fetching relevant documents and adding them to the prompt before the model answers.
Further training an existing model on your own examples to specialise its behaviour.
Model Context Protocol: an open standard for connecting AI models to tools and data sources.
An AI system that works toward a goal in a loop: decide, use a tool, observe, repeat.
Shrinking a model by storing its weights with fewer bits, trading a little quality for much less memory.
The quantum version of a bit. It can be in a blend of 0 and 1 until measured.
A quantum state that is a combination of several possibilities at once.
A seven-layer reference model describing how data moves across a network.
A small unit of data sent across a network, with addressing information attached.
A numeric address that identifies a device on a network.
A smaller network carved out of a larger one.
Notation like /24 that says how many bits of an IP address identify the network.
Domain Name System: translates names like example.com into IP addresses.
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol: automatically hands out IP settings to devices.
Network Address Translation: lets many private addresses share one public IP address.
A device that forwards packets between different networks.
A device that connects devices within one network and forwards frames by MAC address.
A hardware address burned into a network interface, used on the local network.
Virtual LAN: a logically separate network on shared switch hardware.
A number (0-65535) that identifies which service on a device a connection is for.
Virtual Private Cloud: your own isolated network inside a cloud provider.
A service that spreads incoming traffic across several servers.
Infrastructure as a Service: rent virtual machines, storage and networks.
Platform as a Service: deploy your code and the provider runs the servers.
Software as a Service: finished software you use over the internet.
Software that runs multiple virtual machines on one physical computer.
A software computer with its own operating system, running on shared hardware.
A device or program that allows or blocks network traffic according to rules.
A simple, low-detail sketch of a page layout.
Designing pages that adapt to any screen size.
Content Delivery Network: servers around the world that deliver your files from close to each visitor.
A fixed-size fingerprint computed from data. It cannot be reversed.
Random data added to a password before hashing, so identical passwords get different hashes.
Scrambling data so only someone with the right key can read it.
Encryption where the same key locks and unlocks the data.
Encryption using a key pair: a public key to lock and a private key to unlock.
The half of a key pair you can share with anyone.
The half of a key pair you must keep secret.
A signed digital document that ties a public key to an identity such as a domain name.
A trusted organisation that signs certificates.
Multi-Factor Authentication: proving identity with two or more different kinds of evidence.
Role-Based Access Control: permissions are given to roles, and people are assigned roles.
Giving each user or program only the access needed for its job, and nothing more.
Transport Layer Security: the protocol that encrypts connections such as HTTPS.
Secure Shell: an encrypted protocol for logging in to and controlling remote computers.
Tricking someone into revealing secrets or running malware, usually through a fake message.
Intrusion Detection System: watches traffic and raises alerts on suspicious activity.
Intrusion Prevention System: like an IDS, but sits inline and can block traffic.
Security Information and Event Management: collects logs from everywhere and correlates them into alerts.
